scope: Current-canon Phase 1 mobile workshop information architecture only; no gameplay rule, external system, or runtime asset promotion. The current-canon Workshop script receives read-only summaries and native cards only.

entries.applied_rule: Do not turn the single-workpiece Phase 1 slice into workforce, mining, logistics, and shop-management scope.
Use customer/world context only as a same-UID handoff and result return, without a faction-management loop.
Place immediate result feedback beside the single primary mobile action; reject idle/tap-revenue behavior.

entries.source: Blacksmith of the Sand Kingdom official site
entries.applied_rule: Keep crafted equipment meaningful through actual use and result, without adopting party-RPG exploration.

entries.source: While the Iron's Hot official page
entries.applied_rule: Let a workpiece's use have a readable world consequence, but do not add an exploration or puzzle loop.
Use MarginContainer, ScrollContainer, and VBoxContainer for portrait responsive layout ownership.
Centralize repeated Control states in Theme roles rather than scatter visual overrides.

protected_change_gate.why_pending: The local manifest records the user's in-scope authorization, but the Base validator independently requires the PR's approved-protected-change label. No agent self-applies that external approval metadata.

rollback: Revert the native-card implementation and this receipt update. No historical document, runtime scene, image catalog, user save, or Base adoption lock is removed or changed.
project_only_lessons: A text-native blueprint may clarify an approved mobile flow without manufacturing a non-consumed visual asset.
A user request to make needed UI images does not undo an active no-raster boundary unless the exact consumer and visual decision are amended.

A runtime capture can expose mobile hierarchy failures that control-tree and unit checks cannot: use compact player-facing UID text and avoid duplicating a card summary in adjacent non-interactive labels.
